CLINICAL FEATURES OF HEART FAILURE
- Major Diagnostic criteria:
- Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea
- Orthopnoea
- Raised jugular venous pressure
- Pulmonary oedema

- Minor diagnostic criteria include:
- Cough productive of frothy sputum
- Leg swelling
- Abdominal swelling
- The prominence of particular symptoms will depend on which side
is affected
- Oedema
- Tachycardia (about 100 beats per minute)
- Displaced apex
- Hepatomegaly, ascites
A diagnosis of heart failure requires 2 major or 1 major and 2 or more minor
criteria
